findings.title: English reference path derivation breaks for non-resources-community and mangles paths
findings.body: The English counterpart path is computed by regex replacing '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties' with '_en.properties' on the whole absolute path. Any '_' in parent directories (e.g. a checkout path like /home/user/my_repo/...) is not affected since the regex requires '.properties' suffix, but the file-name pattern is applied greedily from the first underscore-containing segment of the filename only; more importantly for files like 'messages_zh_CN.properties' it works, yet for the theme-verifier fixtures (e.g. 'noHtml_de.properties' -> 'noHtml_en.properties') it is fine. The real issue: files under themes/src/main/resources/ (not resources-community) map to themselves only when the locale is en, and for non-community English files the path is unchanged, so verifySafeHtml reads and compares a file to itself. Also if the English file does not exist the code throws RuntimeException, aborting the whole verification instead of reporting a message, which crashes the Maven build for any locale file lacking an English counterpart.

findings.title: Missing English file or IO failure throws RuntimeException instead of reporting
findings.body: verifySafeHtml throws RuntimeException on IOException for both the target file and the English file. verify() only catches IOException, so the RuntimeException escapes the Mojo, producing an unhelpful stack trace rather than a verification message. Keys with no English counterpart are handled, but a missing English file is not.

findings.title: Anchor replacement removes first occurrence anywhere, not at the matched position
findings.body: santizeAnchors uses value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "") which strips the first textual occurrence of the anchor tag, not the one the matcher found. With repeated identical anchors, or when the translation has an anchor text that appears earlier in a different position, the wrong tag is removed and the comparison against the English tag list becomes inconsistent. Also the English matcher is advanced in lockstep with no check that the number of anchors matches, so a translation with fewer anchors passes silently.

findings.title: Policy and pattern fields are package-visible instance fields
findings.body: POLICY_SOME_HTML, POLICY_NO_HTML and HTML_TAGS are non-private, non-static instance fields rebuilt per object. They should be static final constants; the policy factory is relatively expensive to construct and is needlessly recreated for every file verified.

findings.title: Test resources for noHtml/illegalHtmlTag depend on sibling _en files that are not checked for the intended failure
findings.body: verifyNoHtmlAllowed and verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected assert only that 'Illegal HTML' appears, using hasItem. Because verify() also aggregates other messages, these tests could pass for unrelated reasons (e.g. a missing-English-file path or anchor message). Assertions should be specific to the key/file, and the positive case (valid translation with allowed <b> when English has HTML) is not tested.

findings.title: Fixture is unclosed HTML and the test does not verify it is the English file being checked
findings.body: illegalHtmlTag_en.properties contains '<div>tag</div' (missing '>'), which is a malformed tag rather than a clearly illegal one; the test name suggests an illegal tag but the fixture tests a broken closing tag. The fixture is also an English file, so the test exercises the English path only, not a translation comparison.

findings.title: Finnish totpStep1 replaced with a Finnish-less English-Italian placeholder string
findings.body: The Finnish, Lithuanian, Swedish, Slovak and Norwegian account/login translations were replaced with lines that are not translations at all. Here totpStep1 in account messages_fi is replaced with a Finnish sentence that lost its meaning, and in messages_lt.properties totpStep1 is replaced by the Italian string 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. This shows untranslated Italian text to Lithuanian users. The change removes the link to the FreeOTP/Google Play apps instead of fixing the HTML sanitization, which is a content regression rather than a sanitizer fix.

findings.title: Lithuanian account message replaced with Italian text
findings.body: totpStep1 in the Lithuanian account bundle is now 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see Italian in the TOTP setup page. The original Lithuanian translation was removed to satisfy the sanitizer rather than fixing the markup.

findings.title: Lithuanian login loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: loginTotpStep1 is replaced by Italian 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. The Lithuanian translation of the app-install step is lost and Lithuanian users see Italian.

findings.title: Hungarian emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml had a stray *** prefix in the diff context
findings.body: The diff shows the key 'emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml' line prefixed with '***' in the change, which is a corrupt key name; the line in the file would no longer match the key and the Hungarian HTML email body would be unusable/ignored. Verify the key is not corrupted.

findings.title: Lithuanian email href changed from broken to correct but other anchors left malformed
findings.body: The change alters href=LT"..." to href="...", which is correct, but the full file still contains other malformed markup; the sanitizer change masks the original HTML error instead of addressing content that is actually broken in emails.

findings.title: Norwegian identityProviderLinkBody changed by removing HTML and changing meaning
findings.body: identityProviderLinkBody in Norwegian replaces {1} with plain {1}, removing the emphasis. This is an alteration of translated content made to appease a sanitizer rule, not a fix of wrong markup, and it changes the rendered message for the plain-text version too.

findings.title: Dutch emailVerificationBodyHtml unbalanced tag change
findings.body:
The change closes a

with '' typo fixed to '

' which is correct, but the associated diff indicates a broken closing tag was in the original; no validation was added to the verifier to catch this class of error, so the fix relies on manual edits across 40+ files.

findings.title: Bulk whitespace-only edits across many locale files
findings.body:
Dozens of login messages only change '
' to '
'. These are noisy diffs that do not change rendering, obscuring the actual sanitizer-driven content changes such as the Italian/Lithuanian substitutions.

findings.title: Slovak error-invalid-multivalued-size uses wrong argument index in choice
findings.body: The final key in the Slovak file's diff changes the second choice from {1,choice,...} to {2,choice,...} for the maximum count, which is the intended fix, but the original line in the Slovak file ends with a value using {1} for max; the changed line also removes the trailing newline. Also impersonateTitleHtml has an unmatched '' removed, a correct fix, but the diff for the other edits mixes content changes with markup changes in one commit.

findings.title: Czech multivalued-size choice format has inconsistent plural forms
findings.body: error-invalid-multivalued-size in Czech uses choice patterns '0#hodnot|1#hodnotu|1<hodnoty|4<hodnot' which is inconsistent with the other locales and with the English pattern; the value 1 uses 'hodnotu' correctly but the 2-4 case relies on the '1<hodnoty' rule with a '4<' boundary that drops the 2-4 distinction incorrectly.

findings.title: Changed placeholder syntax breaks i18next interpolation in account UI
findings.body: error-invalid-multivalued-size changes from i18next-style {{0}} placeholders to MessageFormat {0} with a choice clause. The account UI is a React/i18next app which interpolates {{...}} and does not evaluate MessageFormat choice syntax, so the rendered message will show the raw '{0}' and '{2,choice,...}' text to users.

findings.title: Admin UI message uses MessageFormat placeholders while the admin UI uses i18next double braces
findings.body: error-invalid-multivalued-size is changed to {0} / {2,choice,...} syntax, but this admin-ui bundle is consumed by i18next which expects {{0}}. Users will see raw placeholders and choice markup in the admin console.

findings.title: Only a whitespace change for CLAIM.<NAME> in Chinese help text
findings.body: The change removes a space before '>' in 'CLAIM.<NAME >' to 'CLAIM.<NAME>'. This is a correction of an unrelated typo that is bundled into a sanitizer change and does not match the sanitizer rationale.

findings.title: Admin theme message switched to MessageFormat choice syntax without matching renderer
findings.body: error-invalid-multivalued-size now uses {2,choice,...} syntax. Other admin messages in this file use plain {n} placeholders consumed by the admin UI; if that UI does not run MessageFormat choice evaluation, users will see literal choice markup.

findings.title: Login theme error-invalid-multivalued-size uses choice format while previous wording 'value(s)' was intended as plural-neutral
findings.body: The English message now emits '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' which requires MessageFormat rendering at the caller. Callers that format with simple substitution will print the raw choice pattern for every locale, and the change is applied to English but other locales (e.g. ka, ko) were given different forms, producing inconsistent behavior.
